top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu alone) is the only proposal with a literary case under the common criteria. On public knowledge, the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid have a distinctive voice and sustained formal ambition. They join memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation in recursive, patterned prose built at large scale over decades. The citation should rest on the major prose and name the poetry as its lyric root, since translated coverage of the poetry and early work is uneven. The attribution is clean: one writer, one language. I have not weighed the six matching round-2 configurations or the unanimous openings as evidence. The open reservations remain: how much Romanian syntax, wordplay and rhythm survives in translation, and whether Solenoid widens the project or restages the trilogy. I have not verified either from the Romanian originals. These reservations are the same ones I would raise against any large-scale prose project. No rival in the record shows a clearly stronger case on voice, form, depth and sustained achievement. Carson would be my fallback if translation proved too weak a basis, but her scope is narrower and harder to fix. P000 is ranked below P001 because the reservations qualify the case without defeating it.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. My scholarly work on modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature and Celan is context only, and the profile records no tie to any shortlisted writer. As chair I wrote the round-1 summary, but that role gives me no extra weight on the merits.
